title: containers.conf [containers] init=true is ignored
body:
### Issue Description

Setting `init=true` under `[containers]` in `containers.conf` does not enable an init process when the `--init` option is omitted.

The [containers.conf](https://github.com/containers/common/blob/main/docs/containers.conf.5.md#containers-table) documentation describes `init`:
> Run an init inside the container that forwards signals and reaps processes.

And explicitly providing `--init=true` does work, demonstrating that the init binary is available. However, the equivalent file-configured default is ignored.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

1. Add the following to `~/.config/containers/containers.conf`:

  ```toml
  [containers]
  init=true
  ```

2. Run the same container with the init option omitted, enabled, and disabled and observe the result:

  ```bash
  printf 'init omitted: '
  podman run --rm docker.io/library/alpine:latest cat /proc/1/comm
  
  printf 'init=true: '
  podman run --rm --init=true docker.io/library/alpine:latest cat /proc/1/comm
  
  printf 'init=false: '
  podman run --rm --init=false docker.io/library/alpine:latest cat /proc/1/comm
  ```

### Describe the results you received

The configured default is ignored when `--init` is omitted:

```text
init omitted: cat
init=true: podman-init
init=false: cat
```

### Describe the results you expected

The container that ran with the `--init` option omitted should inherit `init=true` from `containers.conf`:

```text
init omitted: podman-init
init=true: podman-init
init=false: cat
```

### Podman in a container

No

### Privileged Or Rootless

Rootless

### Upstream Latest Release

Yes

### Additional environment details

I have reproduced the issue on various systems as well as running Podman in a container.

### Additional information

In Podman v6.1.4, the command-line `--init` option appears to be registered with a hard-coded `false` default and does not honor or merge in the value defined in `containers.conf`

https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/blob/v6.1.4/cmd/podman/common/create.go#L181-L185

comments.body: Hi, I'd be happy to give this a go.

@nadav78 Thank you for working on this! 🙌

Does your change also cover containers created through the Docker-compatible socket/API?

For this issue, I provided the simplest reproducible example I could think of. However, I wanted to clarify that my primary use case is Jenkins Docker Plugin communicating with Podman through its socket, in case that makes a difference.

From what I understand, the Jenkins Docker plugin omits `HostConfig.Init`, so I need the server-side `containers.conf` value to apply. As a similar example, I can confirm that another `containers.conf` default, `userns="nomap"`, correctly applies to containers created by Jenkins.

I see that this PR changes the CLI flag default in `cmd/podman/common/create.go`. Could you confirm whether container creation via the Docker-compatible API passes through the same code? I’m not familiar enough with Podman’s internals to fully understand the flow here, but I noticed that the separate `pkg/api/handlers/compat/containers_create.go` appears to turn an omitted `HostConfig.Init` into `false`.

If the API uses a separate flow, could support for the server-side `init` default be included here?
